newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania c.bank February reserves dip to $697.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Romania c.bank February reserves dip to $697.7 mln.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) said on Wednesday total February foreign exchange reserves fell to $697.7 million from $812.2 million at end-January.
Central bank officials told Reuters the slide was triggered by external payments to service the country's foreign debt, which latest data put at $6.9 billion at end-1996.
Last week, foreign exchange dealers said the BNR sold dollars on the market to prop up the leu currency. But the BNR said it had only tested the market, declining to elaborate.
Since, the leu has firmed sharply to near 6,000 to the dollar versus about 9,000 early last week.
BNR data also showed January foreign reserve assets in the banking system fell to $2.77 billion from $3.14 billion at end-1996. Data on February reserve assets were not available.
End-January reserve assets include gold reserves of about 88 tonnes, Special Drawing Rights and the BNR's and local banks' hard currency reserves.

On Tuesday, the lower chamber of parliament set the ceiling for 1997 foreign debt at $3.2 billion in a bill allowing the BNR and the finance ministry to raise and guarantee medium- and long-term loans from world markets to prop up reforms and enhance hard currency reserves.
The bill still needs approval from parliament's upper house.
Romania's external debt servicing is estimated at $1.5 billion in 1997.
